A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same neural-field weight representation work. All main-text and supplementary pages are readable, and methods, results, figures, and proofs can be matched despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, generation, classification, clustering, initialization-sensitivity, and encoder-ablation results on FFHQ and ShapeNet.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds FFHQ interpolation and nearest-neighbor analyses in the supplement.

M1.justification: The multiplicative adaptation, base-model training, asymmetric masking, hierarchical diffusion encoder, and sampling pipeline are retained. Specifying which LoRA factor receives masking clarifies implementation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Section 11 adds cross-instance FFHQ weight interpolation as a test scenario. This differs from v1's connectivity analysis between two fits of the same ShapeNet instance. The datasets, modalities, and original task coverage otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The new Figure 8 includes standalone MLP as a comparator to mLoRA-Asym for cross-instance FFHQ interpolation. Comparator membership in the existing reconstruction, generation, discriminative, and encoder-ablation experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols evaluate linear interpolation between different instances' weight factors and retrieve generated images' nearest training neighbors using CLIP similarity. Existing sample counts, training budgets, generation metrics, and the 2,048-generated/2,048-reference evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 8–9 add qualitative diagnostics of interpolation continuity and possible memorization. The existing initialization-perturbation analysis in Figure 3 and hierarchical encoder ablation in Table 5 are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3 still reports averages over 30 instances with standard-deviation shading. Table 4 retains statistics from 10 runs with random splits and initializations. The added qualitative analyses introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. Newly reported qualitative findings show that cross-instance interpolation is not consistently smooth and that displayed FFHQ generations differ visually from their CLIP-nearest training neighbors.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 adds an explicit GL(r) change-of-basis symmetry identity beyond the earlier permutation discussion. Existing supplementary theorems and proofs are retained. The new identity uses AB ordering, inconsistent with the previously defined BA factor dimensions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims that constrained multiplicative LoRA weights support reconstruction, generation, and semantic discrimination. The added emphasis on independently optimized weights clarifies the existing per-instance fitting approach.

C2.justification: v2 discusses unsuccessful smooth interpolation, interprets nearest-neighbor examples as evidence against memorization, and explicitly limits weight comparisons to a shared base model and initialization. It removes the uniform per-layer parameter-budget limitation while retaining computational-cost and generation-quality limitations.

D1.justification: Section 3.4 now explicitly specifies masking all LoRA A matrices and sharing mask positions across instances and training runs. Section 8 otherwise retains the implementation architectures, hyperparameters, optimization schedules, and dataset preparation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Functa and contrasts its meta-learned shift modulations with independently optimized weights. It refines the distinction from model-agnostic weight encoders and expands the already-cited Dravid discussion in related work. These additions are not evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The title and wording are revised, Section 3.4 is rewritten, and the main INR review is condensed with a fuller supplementary discussion. Limitations and references are relocated, while the central method-to-experiments narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted from a single-column preprint to a two-column main paper and supplement. Figures and tables are resized and relocated; Table 3 changes from stacked to side-by-side dataset blocks. Figures 8–9 are added, while earlier qualitative panels are retained as Figures 10–12.

improvement.justification: The interpolation diagnostic, nearest-neighbor check, explicit shared-base limitation, and Functa comparison improve transparency about evidence and scope. Gains are limited because the method and numerical findings are unchanged. Qualifications remain: the qualitative neighbor panel does not establish absence of memorization, the layer-budget caveat is removed, and the added GL(r) identity has inconsistent factor ordering.
